scope: 128 bounded records/documents (including fixed goldens and contract controls), 64 quote/newline/UTF-8 mutations, 8 writer controls; at most 4 fields and 48 bytes per field; not exhaustive Unicode or fuzzing.

generator.method: Seeded bounded field selection and quoted record construction; 20 Go goldens, 4 csv-core/empty goldens, 10 semantic controls, 74 constructed documents, 12 explicit-width controls, 8 record-bound controls; 64 mutations. Expectations only from upstream oracle plus listed contract adaptations.
generator.chunk_plans: All n+1 one-split positions for inputs <=20 bytes, including empty endpoint chunks; otherwise fixed 1/2/7-byte plans. Identical plans are exercised by feed and refill read_record. Refill callbacks skip zero-length endpoint pieces (zero denotes EOF) and additionally honor the parser request bound; feed exercises endpoint empty chunks explicitly.

deviations.adaptation: Go returns completed earlier records and may return fields with its first error. Wrappers discard partial/error-call data and stop at the first error; all operations return a whole-document Result.
deviations.exact_spec_paragraph:
The record limit counts bytes after CRLF/final-CR normalization, including quotes,
delimiters and quoted newlines, excluding an outside-quote terminator. It is
checked before retaining another normalized byte; at most one CR is held as
lookahead. Zero permits blank lines only. Width is checked per record when
configured; there is no first-record width inference. Positions have one-based
line numbers and byte columns, with the record's starting line. A bad closing
quote points at the quote, and an unclosed field points just past its final
normalized line. UnequalFields points at column 1 of the starting line. UTF-8 may
cross chunks, but every completed field must validate. Header uniqueness is
application policy. Errors are terminal; later calls report Syntax at the current
input position. Go's partial-record/recovery APIs, Comment, LazyQuotes,
TrimLeadingSpace, ReuseRecord and UseCRLF options are outside this API.

deviations.adaptation: Raw Go zero-width requests run with FieldsPerRecord=-1; adapted expected UnequalFields at the first nonempty record. Positive widths use Go directly.

deviations.adaptation: Go preserves BOM as field content; csv-core strips it only when enough bytes are buffered. BOM input is a Go contract control, excluded from common csv-core comparison.
deviations.exact_spec_paragraph:
Delimiters must be nonzero ASCII other than quote/CR/LF. The strict dialect
matches Go `encoding/csv`: fields may be quoted, contain delimiters or newlines,
and escape a quote by doubling it. A quote in an unquoted field or data after a
closing quote is a syntax error. LF terminates records; CRLF is normalized to LF
inside and outside quotes. Bare CR is field data except that a final CR before
EOF is dropped for Go compatibility. Blank lines are skipped, including trailing
blank lines under a width constraint. Quoted empty fields remain records; empty
input has no records. EOF finalizes an unterminated record once, rejecting an
unclosed quote. Empty feeds after EOF are harmless; nonempty feeds return Syntax.

deviations.adaptation: csv-core never errors and defaults to CR/LF/CRLF terminators; quoted CRLF is not Go normalization. Compare only Go-valid LF-only BOM-free tokenization; all other IDs retain an explicit csv_core_disposition.

deviations.adaptation: Writer raw bytes are pinned Go results; preserve mode changes exactly one empty field to quoted empty plus LF. Zero fields stay LF.
deviations.exact_spec_paragraph:
`WriteConfig { delimiter: u8, preserve_single_empty: bool }` controls
`write_record_with`; `default_write_config()` selects comma and false, preserving
all legacy bytes. With `preserve_single_empty: true`, exactly `[""]` appends
`b"\"\"\n"` (two quote bytes and LF), which reparses as one row with one empty
field. Zero-field records (`[]`) still append bare LF and remain indistinguishable
from blank lines. Records with two or more fields and all other quoting,
whitespace and newline rules are unchanged. This is not a general lossless CSV
round-trip policy: the reader still normalizes CRLF.

deviations.adaptation: The matrix selects comma, tab and semicolon, with all optional Go modes disabled. It makes no claim about Unicode delimiters.

observation: Every selected operation executes in Hirsel with host-built input/expected literals. Each engine must match the independent pass transcript, exit 0, no failures, no budget/block/signal and no root trace. A syntax-error Result is an expected completed operation, never a source/V/H/tooling pass. The reference interpreter runs one original ID per source batch at its unchanged 1M-step budget; the other three engines run the four-ID union. HIRSEL_CSV_RETRY_ENGINES=reference explicitly selects pending reference cells for retries; default is all four engines and missing native tooling fails.
layout: vectors.json has input bytes, input SHA256, upstream raw hex fields/errors and separate adapted expected values/SHA256 for every ID; core-raw.tsv retains every common-valid upstream split result. Engine/run receipts and oracle executables remain external.
writer_input_encoding: input_hex is canonical ASCII JSON of the fields list; input_sha256 seals those bytes. Added as provenance metadata after execution; every consumed fields/expected value remains identical to the frozen campaign manifest.
